title: About
description: Cadence started in 2024 as an internal script. Now nine of us work on it full time from Bilbao and Lisbon.

props.title: We built this because our own changelog was three weeks late, every time
props.subtitle: Cadence started in 2024 as an internal script at a company where two of us worked. It turned merged pull requests into a draft so nobody had to write release notes at 6pm on a Friday. Other teams asked for it. Now nine of us work on it full time from Bilbao and Lisbon.

props.title: Where we are, in numbers we can prove
props.subtitle: Four figures with a source each. A round number with no source is decoration, and one implausible one makes a reader doubt the whole page.

items.label: People, all full time
items.description: Two cities, no offices. Everyone on the team page with their real role.

items.label: Workspaces, 214 paying
items.description: We publish both numbers, not only the bigger one. Counted at 1 September 2026

items.label: Since March 2026
items.description: No outside investment. It matters because it is why we can refuse to add tracking.

items.label: Releases shipped
items.description: All of them on our own changelog, which is the product.

props.title: Three decisions, and what each one costs us
props.subtitle: A values section that any company could publish is worth nothing. These are commitments with a price attached — which is the only way to tell whether one is real.

items.title: No tracking in the widget
items.description: The in-app widget sets no third-party cookie and sends nothing to an ad network.
items.footer: Costs us: the attribution reporting three enterprise prospects asked for. We lost two of them.

items.title: Self-hosting stays fully featured
items.description: Nothing is held back to push you onto the hosted plan. SSO is not an upsell.
items.footer: Costs us: roughly a fifth of our revenue sits on a plan we cannot upsell.

items.title: We tell you when we are the wrong tool
items.description: If you ship quarterly, our pricing page says a wiki page is enough. It is on the page, not buried in a call.
items.footer: Costs us: signups. Gains us: a support load a nine-person team can carry.
